references.text: Judas Iscariot is referred to here as the one who would betray Jesus, and he is identified as one of the twelve disciples, just as in John 6:71.
The text confirms that it was Satan who entered Judas, who was one of the twelve, and who would betray Jesus, which directly connects to the prophecy in John 6:71.
Jesus refers to Judas as the one who went astray, noting that he was one of the twelve, summarizing the role described in John 6:71.
Matthew describes Judas Iscariot as one of the twelve who went to the chief priests to betray Jesus, an action foretold in John 6:71.
Mark tells us that Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests to betray Jesus, confirming the identity and action mentioned in John 6:71.
Luke describes how Satan entered Judas, who was one of the twelve, and that he agreed to betray Jesus, a direct fulfillment of the prophecy in John 6:71.
